writers.notes: GRAIN MISMATCH, the load-bearing note for this writer: the registered contract has NO list field — its two required fields are OBJECT MAPS, pillars {P1..P4: {score, peer_median, source_cell}} and categories {PxCy: {score, peer_median, source_cell}}, so item_field is null. The writer fans BOTH maps into rows, one row per map entry: pillar rows set pillar_id from the map key; category rows set category_id from the map key and pillar_id from its Px prefix; each row takes score, peer_median, source_cell from the entry (source_cell is mandatory in the contract — a figure naming no workbook location is rejected). The DDL mirrors the Surface Spec's per-subcap H4 cell shape, so the subcap-grain columns (subcap_id, name, capability_id, peer_n, peer_basis, confidence, is_thin_evidence, below_threshold, is_primary_gap) have no source in the current contract and stay NULL on aggregate rows; if the grid's 851 subcap rows are meant to be served from this table they must arrive as workbook pass-through from the ingested subcap_scores register (the DDL's own comment on `score` says 'workbook pass-through; authoritative for the grid') — ADJUDICATE before freezing. rollup_score and score_source are APP-COMPUTED at serve time (workbook_scores.resolve_cell), never stored. Payload carries no band and no colour (invariant 7); band and delta are GENERATED. Page-level: contracts_data's _narrative_thread_note says no source names the heatmap lead section — narrative_thread stays NULL on every heatmap section pending adjudication (the page table lists workbook_scores first; the D3 thread opens with focus areas).

columns.source: skip:hoisted at read from series[].basis — the contract states basis PER POINT only and mixing definitions across periods is prohibited, so the set has cardinality 1. A section-level basis would be a SECOND place the metric definition is stated, which is how two definitions come to disagree. Validation asserts one distinct basis across the series rather than storing a hoist; live-adapter hoists it for the card.

skip:computed at read from series[].period/value (invariants 8 and 9) — no source states a CAGR arithmetic, a threshold or a payload key; the only mention rides on STEP 6's 'computed from the series'. `trend` differs because no doc gives a VOLATILE-vs-STABLE threshold, so only the producer can state that. A producer-stated, cited CAGR belongs on O2 firmographics.fields[], whose must-present set names CAGR — not here. The adapter's cagrOf() computes it from the first and last dated points over the real number of years between them, returning nothing when fewer than two dated points exist.

writers.notes: O8 + C6 (one section, two surfaces — the DDL comment says 'serves O8 and C6'; the two cards cannot disagree). series JSONB stores the points [{period, value, unit, as_of, source_e_id, basis}] oldest first. One row per cards[] item (I1; contract mandates 6-10 cards — zero cards on a completed run is a FAILURE STATE at validation, so an empty write here is never legitimate for a completed run). NAME MAPPING: envelope column e_ids is filled from the card's supporting_e_ids[] (contract key differs from column name). Rationale: supporting_e_ids[] is mandatory per card ('the serve layer excludes uncited cards'), the table has no other evidence column, contracts_data _notes adjudicate supporting_e_ids as the per-card form of cards[].e_ids, and the item-grain convention in 0008 stores the ITEM's citation list in e_ids (heatmap_cell_evidence.grounded_on is GENERATED from e_ids per row — invariant 8 only works per-item). Consequence: the section-envelope e_ids union is NOT separately stored on this table; it remains in the retained staged submission and is reconstructible as the union of row e_ids. If env:e_ids were used instead, per-card citations would be lost at promotion — flagged for adjudication. writers.notes: NAME MISMATCH: contract item key is `product`, column is `name` — the contract's own _notes record that the TRD representative contract called this field `name` while the Surface Spec/skill REISSUED prompt use `product` (vendor and product are separate fields; product wins in the payload); the DDL kept the TRD spelling `name`, so the writer maps item.product -> name. NO-ITEM-KEY COLUMN: `is_primary_gap` is not in the item shape — it is carried per layer in the section-level `layers[]` rollup ({layer, pillar_id, detected, expected, is_primary_gap}); the writer fills each row by matching item.layer to its layers[] entry and copying that entry's is_primary_gap flag (matches the §06 DDL comment on techstack_items placing the flag per row). E_IDS: on this item-grain table the row-level `e_ids` takes each item's own e_ids[] (the contract requires every item to cite the evidence placing it in the estate — an uncitable item goes to dropped[]), not the section-envelope union; same item-over-section rule as r_layer. CONTRACT FIELDS WITH NO COLUMN: (a) item key `as_of` has no column and this table has no JSONB payload carrier — it is validated in the payload but not persisted, flag if row-level dating is later needed; (b) section field `layers[]` is not stored beyond the per-row is_primary_gap derivation — the T2 landscape strip and the four layer cards recompute detected-of-expected counts from this register at read (invariant 8, and insights_landscape.summary's comment says counts are NEVER stored); (c) section field `dropped[]` ({candidate, reason}) has no column — not persisted in the serving tier by this writer; (d) optional `compliance_attestations[]` (plain strings) has no column — not persisted here. NARRATIVE_THREAD: the techstack section contract declares no narrative_thread field; the skill puts the page-level thread on each page's lead section and techstack has exactly one section, so if the payload carries one it lands here via the envelope path — NULL is correct when absent. R_LAYER: items do not carry r_layer, so section-level (nullable, NULL when the section has none). STATUS is the table's only payload NOT NULL — CONFIRMED|INFERRED|CLAIMED|ABSENT required per row because the landscape strip recomputes its four counts from this column. UNIQUENESS: 0008 creates UNIQUE INDEX techstack_items_ts_uq ON (run_id, ts_id) — ts_id is agent-minted (TS-nnn) and must be unique within the run, so delete-then-insert ordering inside the promote transaction matters. GENERATED columns: none on this table. DROPPED (0023): section-grain on an item-grain table, repeated per row and read once — the same shape overview_firmographics uses for sub_vertical_undefined. The sibling required field `layers` is deliberately NOT bound: every ingredient of the rollup is on these item rows, so it is recomputed at read (invariant 8) and a column would be a second answer that could disagree with the rows beneath it.
